segments.text: This is Byte. Byte just ordered the biggest burger in town.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) at a diner counter, a giant burger on a plate in front of him, excited face, warm diner lights
E: same scene and camera, Byte licks his lips and rubs his hands together

segments.text: He taps his card. Declined.
shots: B: close-up of Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) tapping a bank card on a card reader that shows a big red X, diner counter
E: same scene, Byte's eyes go wide in shock, sweat drop on his head

segments.text: No cash. No coins. Nothing. Just a very hungry stickman.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) turning his empty hoodie pockets inside out, a moth flying out, diner background
E: same scene, Byte looks sadly at the burger, stomach rumbling lines

segments.text: The cook looks at his hoodie and says: I'll take that instead.
shots: S: a stickman cook with dot eyes and a small mouth, white chef hat and apron, pointing at someone's teal hoodie with a cheeky grin, diner kitchen behind
B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) hugging his teal hoodie protectively, horrified face, diner counter

segments.text: Wait. Can you really just trade stuff? For most of history, there were no coins, no cards, no apps.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) scratching his head with a thought bubble showing a goat, a coin and a phone, plain warm background

segments.text: So how did we go from swapping goats... to paying with numbers on a screen?
shots: S: a stickman farmer with dot eyes and a small mouth in a straw hat holding a rope tied to a goat, dusty ancient field
S: a stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a modern hoodie tapping a glowing smartphone on a payment terminal, sleek shop

segments.text: Let's go back. Way back.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) being sucked into a swirling time portal full of flying coins and banknotes, comedic panic

segments.text: Here's the story you probably learned at school. Before money, people bartered.
shots: S: a stickman teacher with dot eyes and a small mouth in a brown cardigan pointing at a chalkboard drawing of a goat and a sack of wheat with arrows between them, classroom

segments.text: I have a goat. You have wheat. We swap.
shots: S: two stickmen with dot eyes and a small mouth in an ancient village, one in a straw hat holding a goat on a rope, the other in a red tunic holding a sack of wheat, facing each other
E: same scene and camera, the two stickmen shake hands over the goat and the wheat

segments.text: But what if I don't want a goat?
shots: S: close-up of a stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a red tunic crossing his arms and shaking his head at a goat, unimpressed, village background
E: same scene, the goat looks offended

segments.text: Economists call this the double coincidence of wants. You need someone who has what you want, and wants what you have.
shots: S: a stickman merchant with dot eyes and a small mouth in a green robe walking through a market with a goat, thought bubbles of a pot, shoes and a chicken, small distant stalls
E: same scene, the merchant looks exhausted, sweat drops, the goat chewing his sleeve

segments.text: Here's the twist. Anthropologists have never found a society that ran purely on barter.
shots: S: a stickman explorer with dot eyes and a small mouth in a khaki pith helmet holding a notebook and a magnifying glass, shrugging, jungle village behind
E: same scene, the explorer crosses out the word barter in his notebook

segments.text: In small villages, people did something simpler. They kept track of favours.
shots: S: a stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a blue tunic handing a basket of bread to a neighbour stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a yellow tunic, cosy village street

segments.text: You give me bread today. I owe you one. Everybody remembers.
shots: S: the stickman in a yellow tunic with dot eyes and a small mouth giving a thumbs up while a tally mark glows on a wooden post beside him, village street

segments.text: In other words, debt came before coins.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) looking at the viewer with a raised eyebrow, a big glowing IOU note floating beside him, plain warm background

segments.text: About five thousand years ago, in Mesopotamia, temples kept track of who owed what.
shots: S: a stickman scribe with dot eyes and a small mouth in a white wrap and headband pressing marks into a clay tablet with a reed, mud-brick temple and ziggurat behind, golden light
E: same scene and camera, the scribe proudly holds up the finished tablet

segments.text: They wrote it down on clay tablets. Some of the oldest writing in the world isn't poetry. It's receipts.
shots: S: close-up of a clay tablet covered in neat wedge-shaped marks lying on a wooden table, warm lamp light, no people
S: a stickman farmer with dot eyes and a small mouth in a straw hat reading a clay tablet with a shocked face, sacks of barley behind him

segments.text: Debts were counted in barley, and in silver, weighed in a unit called the shekel.
shots: S: a stickman merchant with dot eyes and a small mouth in a striped robe weighing small pieces of silver on a balance scale next to sacks of barley, market stall

segments.text: A shekel wasn't a coin. It was a weight. About eight grams of silver.
shots: S: close-up of a bronze balance scale with a small pile of silver on one side and a stone weight on the other, plain warm background, no people

segments.text: Far away, people found other things to count with. Shells.
shots: S: a stickman trader with dot eyes and a small mouth in a colourful wrap holding a string of white cowrie shells, tropical beach and a wooden boat behind

segments.text: Cowrie shells were small, tough and hard to fake. They were used as money across Asia, Africa and the Indian Ocean for centuries.
shots: S: close-up of a pile of shiny white cowrie shells spilling out of a woven basket, warm light, no people
S: two stickmen with dot eyes and a small mouth at a busy harbour market, one in a blue wrap handing cowrie shells to the other in an orange wrap who holds a basket of fish

segments.text: In Chinese writing, the old symbol for a shell even became part of the words for money and buying.
shots: S: a stickman scholar with dot eyes and a small mouth in a dark blue robe and black cap painting a large simple shell-shaped symbol on a paper scroll with a brush, Chinese study room

segments.text: And on the tiny Pacific island of Yap, money was enormous.
shots: S: a giant round stone disc with a hole in the middle standing upright in a tropical village, a tiny stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a grass skirt beside it for scale, palm trees

segments.text: Giant stone discs called rai. The biggest are about three and a half metres wide, and weigh around four tonnes.
shots: S: a stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a grass skirt trying to push a huge round stone disc, straining, sweat drops, palm trees
E: same scene, the stone hasn't moved at all and the stickman sits down exhausted

segments.text: They were carved on another island, hundreds of kilometres away, and brought home by canoe and raft.
shots: S: a huge stone disc on a bamboo raft towed by an outrigger canoe with one stickman paddler with dot eyes and a small mouth, open blue ocean, big waves

segments.text: They were far too heavy to move. So nobody moved them. Everyone just remembered who owned which stone.
shots: S: two stickmen with dot eyes and a small mouth in grass skirts shaking hands in front of a big stone disc that stays where it is, village elders watching from far away

segments.text: The story goes that one stone sank to the bottom of the sea on the way home. The family still counted it as theirs.
shots: S: a giant stone disc resting on the sandy sea floor with fish swimming around it, sunbeams through the water, no people
S: a stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a grass skirt proudly pointing down at the sea from a beach, a small family beside him smiling

segments.text: Money that nobody can see... but everybody agrees exists. Remember that. It comes back later.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) tapping the side of his head knowingly, winking at the viewer, plain warm background

segments.text: Around six hundred B.C., in a kingdom called Lydia, in what's now Turkey, someone had a brilliant idea.
shots: S: a stickman king with dot eyes and a small mouth with a golden crown and purple robe on a throne, a lightbulb glowing above his head, ancient palace with columns

segments.text: Take lumps of electrum, a natural mix of gold and silver, and stamp them with a lion's head.
shots: S: a stickman metalworker with dot eyes and a small mouth in a leather apron hammering a stamp onto a small golden lump on an anvil, sparks, forge glow
S: close-up of a small lumpy gold coin stamped with a roaring lion's head, on a dark cloth, no people

segments.text: The stamp meant: the king guarantees it. No more weighing.
shots: S: a stickman shopkeeper with dot eyes and a small mouth in a striped tunic happily accepting a small gold coin, tossing his balance scale aside, market stall

segments.text: These were some of the first coins in history.
shots: S: a few small ancient gold and silver coins glowing on a museum display stand, dark background, spotlight, no people

segments.text: A later king of Lydia, Croesus, made coins of pure gold and pure silver. People still say 'rich as Croesus'.
shots: S: a stickman king with dot eyes and a small mouth with a big golden crown sitting on a mountain of gold coins, laughing, treasure room
E: same scene, the king throws coins in the air like confetti

segments.text: Coins spread to Greece, Persia and Rome. Soon, rulers were putting their own faces on them.
shots: S: a stickman emperor with dot eyes and a small mouth in a laurel wreath and toga admiring a coin with a stickman head on it, Roman forum behind
E: same scene, the emperor kisses the coin proudly

segments.text: But coins have a problem. They're heavy.
shots: S: a stickman merchant with dot eyes and a small mouth in a Chinese robe bent over carrying a huge sack of coins on his back, struggling up a road, mountains behind

segments.text: In Sichuan, in China, people used iron coins worth so little that a big purchase needed a whole cart of them.
shots: S: a stickman merchant with dot eyes and a small mouth in a blue Chinese robe pushing a wooden cart overloaded with strings of round iron coins with square holes, busy old Chinese street, a few tiny distant figures

segments.text: So merchants left their coins with trusted shops, and carried paper receipts instead.
shots: S: a stickman merchant with dot eyes and a small mouth handing a heavy chest of coins over a counter to a stickman shopkeeper with dot eyes and a small mouth in a red robe who hands back a paper note, old Chinese shop

segments.text: In ten twenty-four, the Song government took over, and printed the world's first official paper money. The jiaozi.
shots: S: a stickman official with dot eyes and a small mouth in a red Song dynasty robe and black winged hat holding up a large printed paper banknote, wooden printing blocks on a table
S: close-up of an old printed paper banknote with simple patterns and a red seal stamp, no readable text, on a wooden table, no people

segments.text: When Marco Polo saw paper money in China, he could hardly believe it. Paper, worth as much as gold.
shots: S: a stickman traveller with dot eyes and a small mouth in a medieval European cap and cloak staring in amazement at a paper banknote in his hands, Chinese palace courtyard

segments.text: But printing money is tempting. Print too much, and prices explode. That's inflation.
shots: S: a stickman official with dot eyes and a small mouth in a red robe happily cranking a printing press that spits out piles of paper notes
S: a stickman shopper with dot eyes and a small mouth in a blue robe holding a huge stack of paper notes for one tiny bun at a food stall, shocked face

segments.text: Europe caught up much later. In sixteen sixty-one, a bank in Sweden printed Europe's first banknotes.
shots: S: a stickman banker with dot eyes and a small mouth in a black 1600s coat and white collar proudly holding up a paper banknote, wood-panelled bank office, snowy window

segments.text: For centuries, a banknote was a promise. Take it to the bank, and swap it for real gold or silver.
shots: S: a stickman customer with dot eyes and a small mouth in a brown coat handing a paper note across a bank counter to a stickman clerk with dot eyes and a small mouth in a black vest who slides back a gold coin

segments.text: That's called the gold standard.
shots: S: a bank vault full of neatly stacked shiny gold bars, a heavy round vault door open, dramatic light, no people

segments.text: Then, in nineteen seventy-one, the United States ended the link between the dollar and gold.
shots: S: a stickman president with dot eyes and a small mouth in a dark suit at a desk speaking into microphones, an American flag behind him, 1970s office
E: same scene, the president snips a chain connecting a dollar bill to a gold bar with big scissors

segments.text: Since then, most money is backed by one thing. Trust.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) holding a dollar-like green banknote up to the light with a suspicious squint, plain warm background

segments.text: In nineteen fifty, a card called Diners Club let people eat now and pay later. It's often called the first modern credit card.
shots: S: a stickman businessman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a 1950s grey suit and hat proudly showing a small paper card to a waiter stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a bow tie, fancy 1950s restaurant

segments.text: Then came cash machines, online banking, and tapping your phone.
shots: S: a stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a 1970s orange jacket taking cash from an old ATM machine in a brick wall
S: a stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a modern green jacket tapping a smartphone on a payment terminal in a coffee shop

segments.text: And here's the wild part. In the UK, banknotes and coins are only about three percent of all money.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) staring at a giant pie chart where only a tiny slice is coins and notes, jaw dropped, plain warm background

segments.text: The rest is just numbers, sitting in bank computers.
shots: S: glowing rows of green numbers flowing between big server racks in a dark data centre, no people

segments.text: Just like the stones of Yap. Money nobody can see... that everybody agrees exists.
shots: S: a giant stone disc made of glowing digital numbers standing in a tropical village at night, palm trees, no people

segments.text: In two thousand nine, someone using the name Satoshi Nakamoto launched Bitcoin. Money with no bank at all.
shots: S: a mysterious stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a dark hoodie typing on a laptop in a dark room, a big glowing golden coin with a B symbol floating above the screen

segments.text: A year later, a programmer paid ten thousand bitcoins for two pizzas. Years later, those coins were worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
shots: S: a stickman programmer with dot eyes and a small mouth in glasses and a t-shirt happily holding two pizza boxes at his front door, a delivery stickman with dot eyes and a small mouth in a red cap beside him
E: same scene, the programmer's eyes go wide as glowing golden coins fly out of the pizza boxes

segments.text: Which brings us back to Byte.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) at the diner counter clutching his teal hoodie, the burger still in front of him, nervous face

segments.text: He opens his banking app. Turns out, he just forgot to move money onto his card.
shots: B: close-up of Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) looking at his phone screen and facepalming, diner background
E: same scene, Byte grinning sheepishly at the viewer

segments.text: Tap. Paid. In less than a second.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) tapping his phone on the card reader which shows a big green tick, triumphant face, diner counter

segments.text: Five thousand years of clay, shells, stones, gold and paper...
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) biting into the giant burger, blissful face, floating icons of a clay tablet, a shell, a stone disc, a gold coin and a banknote around him

segments.text: all so Byte could buy a burger with a number on a screen.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) leaning back on his diner stool with an empty plate, satisfied, giving the viewer a thumbs up

segments.text: Subscribe to ByteSized AI, and next time, we'll find out how humans invented something else you use every day.
shots: B: Byte (the only stickman in an orange cap and teal hoodie) waving goodbye at the viewer outside the diner at sunset, neon diner sign without words

meta.hook_line: For most of history there were no coins, no cards and no apps. So how did we end up paying with numbers on a screen?
meta.summary: From the barter myth to Bitcoin: clay receipts in Mesopotamia, cowrie shells, the four-tonne stone money of Yap, the first coins of Lydia, China's paper money, the gold standard, credit cards, and why only about 3% of money is cash.
